The test image shows a close-up macro shot of plant tissue covered with dense, fibrous/cottony gray-white mycelial growth, with dark spots/structures visible throughout. This strongly suggests a fungal disease with prominent mycelium. Top candidates: Gray Mold, Sclerotinia Timber Rot, Rhizopus Soft Rots, Southern Blight.

Now viewing one reference from each top candidate:

The match is clear. The Rhizopus_Soft_Rots reference (Bugwood_2.jpg, ID 5369124) is nearly identical to the test image (ID 5369123) — both are sequential Bugwood IDs from the same series showing:
- Dense gray-white fibrous mycelium (Rhizopus stolonifer hyphae/sporangiophores)
- Scattered dark round sporangia throughout
- Same macro close-up style on tomato tissue

The other candidates (Gray Mold showed cracked fruit with less dense mycelium; Sclerotinia showed wilted stems; Rhizopus microscopic reference showed black sporangia) all differ. The fibrous mycelium with distinct black sporangia pins perfectly matches Rhizopus Soft Rots.
